why: Every merge's sum is paid again in every later merge it takes part in, so small numbers should be combined first: this is the Huffman / connect-ropes greedy, implemented with a min-heap.
hints: A value merged early is counted again in every later merge. Which values should be merged first?
Always merge the two smallest current values; an exchange argument shows any other choice costs at least as much.
Min-heap: pop two, add their sum to the cost, push the sum back, until one value remains. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Sorting once and merging left to right is wrong: a merged sum may be larger than later elements.
With n = 2 the cost is just the sum of both.
Cost can exceed 32 bits for large n; use 64-bit outside Python.
